back: Cutting and removing material from stock form — material is lost.
Building up a shape by adding material, e.g. 3D printing, with very little waste.
Scratches a fine, accurate line on metal.
Mark lines parallel to an edge.
Makes a small dent to locate a drill bit at the centre of a hole.
A straight, true reference edge that all marking out is measured from.
Pilot hole: small hole to guide a screw and stop splitting. Clearance hole: large enough for the screw to pass through without the thread gripping.
A hole flared at the top so a screw head sits flush with the surface.
Welding, brazing, soldering, riveting and epoxy resin adhesives.
Nuts, bolts and washers, machine screws, self-tapping screws, hinges and catches.
Joining with a brass spelter at bright red heat, using flux, without melting the parent metal; the filler flows in by capillary action.
Drill a clearance hole, insert the rivet, squeeze the rivet gun to pull the mandrel until it snaps. Useful when only one side of the joint can be reached.
A lathe turns metal to make round parts; a milling machine cuts slots and faces off edges.
Temporary fittings such as cam locks, corner blocks and scan fittings, used in flat-pack furniture.
A very strong box joint where flared 'fingers' fit into matching shapes cut in the other piece.
A very strong frame joint where a square tenon is glued into a square mortise.
Gluing a thin slice of attractive timber onto a cheaper, stable base such as MDF.
Gluing thin strips with the grain the same way and clamping them around a former until set, giving a strong curve.
Heating solid timber in a steam box, bending it around a former and clamping until dry.
Heating a narrow line across thermoforming sheet on a strip heater, bending it and holding it in a jig until cool.
Dissolves the surfaces of acrylic so they fuse as the solvent evaporates.
A CAD model is sliced into layers and filament (PLA, ABS) is melted through a nozzle layer by layer. Good for prototypes; slow with visible layer lines.
Pressing a shape into card so it is raised (embossed) or sunken (debossed).
Trimming printed sheets to final size along the crop marks, removing the bleed.
